input_check.note: These checks test physical consistency (rigid 3-D scene, motion matching GPS, metadata agreeing with telemetry). They can expose fabricated or mismatched inputs, but no software can certify that footage is genuine.

processes.what: Picks the frames to reconstruct from, targeting a set overlap between neighbours so every surface is seen from several angles without processing thousands of near-identical frames.
processes.covers: Measured overlap between consecutive kept frames, how many frames were kept, and the selection time against its budget.
processes.lacks: It cannot know whether the flight itself covered the whole site: a strip the drone never flew over is reported later, as a gap.

processes.what: Rejects frames whose motion blur would push wrong geometry into the reconstruction, and marks mildly soft frames for sharpening instead.
processes.covers: The share of frames rejected, and whether the sharpness threshold adapted to the clip rather than being fixed.
processes.lacks: Blur is judged on the whole frame, so a sharp frame with one blurred moving object is kept; the moving object is handled by dynamic masking instead.

processes.what: Keeps brightness consistent across the flight, lifts shadow detail and marks shadowed pixels so they carry less weight when surfaces are matched.
processes.covers: The exposure correction actually applied, whether any frame was driven to its limit, the share of the frame in shadow and the share of blown-out pixels in the written frames.
processes.lacks: Shadow detection has no per-pixel ground truth on real footage, so its precision is measured on synthetic scenes rather than on this clip.

processes.what: Runs a learned depth model over the frames and pins its output to the measured geometry, adding detail in areas where stereo matching alone is thin.

processes.lacks: Learned depth is only accepted where it agrees with measurement; where it disagrees it is refused, which protects accuracy but limits how much it can add.

projection.basis: Times scale with the number of frames kept, which scales with the length of the flight, so each measured time is multiplied by 10 minutes divided by this clip's length. Accuracy and coverage figures are properties of the flight and do not change with clip length.

coverage.source: Stage 3 zone map (zone 1 + zone 2 of the ground the cameras saw)

zones.note: zone 1 = measured, >= zone1_min_views at a sufficient angle; zone 2 = thin or monocular (anchored, weight < zone 1); zone 3 = never observed, listed in gaps.geojson, never filled

limitations: Speed: 44.2 min for 1.7 min of video projects to 256 min for a 10-minute video against the §9 target of 15 min (device cuda; S4-8).
Camera centres agree with GPS to 2.136 m RMS: absolute position is limited by the telemetry; relative distances within Zone 1 are more reliable.
12.0% of the ground the cameras saw was never observed (Zone 3): flagged in gaps.geojson and the viewer, never filled, excluded from accuracy.
No independent reference surface was given for this run: accuracy is agreement with the telemetry, not with ground truth (pass --reference with a lidar DSM or LAS).
The degradation benchmark was not run for this report (python -m src.cli bench degrade).
The single-pass simulation needs a multi-strip survey; not run for this report.

obj: The textured surface as plain text geometry: the most widely accepted mesh format, opened by every 3D package.
ply: Every reconstructed point with its colour and its per-point confidence and zone layers.
las: The survey-industry point format, classified into ground, above ground and low noise, and tiled for large sites.
geotiff: A height model and a true-colour orthophoto, both carrying the coordinate system so they drop straight into any GIS.
glb: The web and game-engine format: geometry and texture in one file, used by the viewer on this page.
fbx: The interchange format for Blender, 3ds Max, Maya and Unreal.
